2026-05-08T08:56:49.1920486Z   pr_body: ## Summary

- GitHub's GraphQL `closingIssuesReferences` only resolves closing keywords for PRs targeting the default branch, so orchestrator-managed PRs (base = `orchestrator/project-<n>`) systematically lose linked-issue context for the editor and every reviewer across every autofix iteration.
- When the GraphQL fetch returns `[]`, parse the PR body for explicit `Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves` + `#N` or in-repo issue URL references (same regex as the smoke-test detection step) and back-fill issue title+body via `gh api repos/.../issues/<n>`.
- Scope is intentionally narrow: only `LINKED_ISSUE_CONTEXT_FILE` (editor/reviewer prompt context) is back-filled. `LINKED_ISSUES_JSON` (downstream labeling and auto-merge gating) keeps GraphQL-only semantics — labeling-by-keyword is itself default-branch-gated by GitHub, so back-filling there would alter unrelated semantics.

`tele-funtoken-msg-scoring#2799`, run `25538571413`: PR body contains `Closes <issue-url>` for `#2798`, but the autofix log shows `Linked issue context bytes: 23` (literal placeholder `No linked issues found.`) on all four iterations because the PR's b

2026-05-08T08:56:39.9090604Z   pr_title: fix(review_autofix): back-fill linked-issue context from PR body when GraphQL returns empty
2026-05-08T08:56:39.9104142Z   pr_body: ## Summary

- GitHub's GraphQL `closingIssuesReferences` only resolves closing keywords for PRs targeting the default branch, so orchestrator-managed PRs (base = `orchestrator/project-<n>`) systematically lose linked-issue context for the editor and every reviewer across every autofix iteration.
- When the GraphQL fetch returns `[]`, parse the PR body for explicit `Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves` + `#N` or in-repo issue URL references (same regex as the smoke-test detection step) and back-fill issue title+body via `gh api repos/.../issues/<n>`.
- Scope is intentionally narrow: only `LINKED_ISSUE_CONTEXT_FILE` (editor/reviewer prompt context) is back-filled. `LINKED_ISSUES_JSON` (downstream labeling and auto-merge gating) keeps GraphQL-only semantics — labeling-by-keyword is itself default-branch-gated by GitHub, so back-filling there would alter unrelated semantics.

## Reproducer (live)

`tele-funtoken-msg-scoring#2799`, run `25538571413`: PR body contains `Closes <issue-url>` for `#2798`, but the autofix log shows `Linked issue context bytes: 23` (literal placeholder `No linked issues found.`) on all four iterations because the PR's base is `orchestrator/project-2791`, not `main`.

## Files changed

- GitHub's GraphQL `closingIssuesReferences` only resolves closing keywords for PRs targeting the default branch, so orchestrator-managed PRs (base = `orchestrator/project-<n>`) systematically lose linked-issue context for the editor and every reviewer across every autofix iteration.

2026-05-08T07:52:12.8129972Z   pr_title: fix(review_autofix): back-fill linked-issue context from PR body when GraphQL returns empty
2026-05-08T07:52:12.8157442Z   pr_body: ## Summary

- GitHub's GraphQL `closingIssuesReferences` only resolves closing keywords for PRs targeting the default branch, so orchestrator-managed PRs (base = `orchestrator/project-<n>`) systematically lose linked-issue context for the editor and every reviewer across every autofix iteration.
- When the GraphQL fetch returns `[]`, parse the PR body for explicit `Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves` + `#N` or in-repo issue URL references (same regex as the smoke-test detection step) and back-fill issue title+body via `gh api repos/.../issues/<n>`.
- Scope is intentionally narrow: only `LINKED_ISSUE_CONTEXT_FILE` (editor/reviewer prompt context) is back-filled. `LINKED_ISSUES_JSON` (downstream labeling and auto-merge gating) keeps GraphQL-only semantics — labeling-by-keyword is itself default-branch-gated by GitHub, so back-filling there would alter unrelated semantics.

## Reproducer (live)

`tele-funtoken-msg-scoring#2799`, run `25538571413`: PR body contains `Closes <issue-url>` for `#2798`, but the autofix log shows `Linked issue context bytes: 23` (literal placeholder `No linked issues found.`) on all four iterations because the PR's base is `orchestrator/project-2791`, not `main`.

## Files changed

- `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:1431-1483` — new body-text fallback block; the existing python file write at `1487` now reads `_linked_context_raw` instead of `_linked_raw`.

## Safety

- URL alternative in the regex is restricted to `${{ github.repository }}` — a cross-repo `Closes <other-repo>/issues/N` cannot route an unrelated number into this repo's lookup.
- API cost bounded by the count of distinct closing references in the PR body (typically 1-2); each match issues one REST call.
- All failures are logged and skipped (fail-open). The fallback never blocks the workflow.
- `LINKED_ISSUES_JSON` env var unchanged → no imp

2026-05-07T10:41:57.7865849Z   pr_body: ## Summary

The implement / review_autofix editor / orchestrate_poll conflict-resolver phases were defaulting to `openai/gpt-5.3-codex`, which has the announce-without-emit regression documented at openai/codex#11151. Two recent runs on issues #205 and #204 hit it on attempts 1 AND 2, tripped the empty_streak bail, and shipped no edits — the broadened `ANNOUNCE_EDIT_REGEX` detection works as designed but cannot fix the upstream model behavior.

This PR swaps every workflow / script default to `openai/gpt-5.4` (already used for clarify, plan, validate, judge), retunes the prompts and system instructions to align with the GPT-5.4 prompt guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-guidance), and tags every historical 5.3-codex reference in code comments as "legacy" so future readers don't conflate them with current behavior.

`gpt-5.3-codex` stays in `scripts/codex_model_catalog.json` at `priority: 3` for explicit opt-in via `WORKFLOW_EDITOR_MODEL`. `gpt-5.4` is promoted to `priority: 1`.

2026-05-07T10:41:50.4773970Z   pr_body: ## Summary

The implement / review_autofix editor / orchestrate_poll conflict-resolver phases were defaulting to `openai/gpt-5.3-codex`, which has the announce-without-emit regression documented at openai/codex#11151. Two recent runs on issues #205 and #204 hit it on attempts 1 AND 2, tripped the empty_streak bail, and shipped no edits — the broadened `ANNOUNCE_EDIT_REGEX` detection works as designed but cannot fix the upstream model behavior.

This PR swaps every workflow / script default to `openai/gpt-5.4` (already used for clarify, plan, validate, judge), retunes the prompts and system instructions to align with the GPT-5.4 prompt guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-guidance), and tags every historical 5.3-codex reference in code comments as "legacy" so future readers don't conflate them with current behavior.

`gpt-5.3-codex` stays in `scripts/codex_model_catalog.json` at `priority: 3` for explicit opt-in via `WORKFLOW_EDITOR_MODEL`. `gpt-5.4` is promoted to `priority: 1`.

## What changed (by area)

### Active model defaults (every site flipped to `openai/gpt-5.4`)

- `.github/workflows/implement.yml` — `MODEL_EDITOR`
- `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` — `MODEL_EDITOR`
- `.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml` — `MODEL_CONFLICT_RESOLVER`
- `scripts/validate_process.sh` — `MODEL_EDITOR` fallback
- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` — both inline `${MODEL_EDITOR:-…}` fallbacks
- `scripts/codex_model_catalog.json` — `gpt-5.4` priority 2→1, `gpt-5.3-codex` priority 1→3
- `scripts/write_codex_config.sh` — usage example updated

### Prompt / system-instructions retune (gpt-5.4 prompt guide alignment)
